blockers.title: OS ABI can bypass the pathless binding, whose subject is still not a closed per-scheme identity
evidence: v17 required every member of pathlessClasses (OS ABI) to use volumeConstraint PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED and explained that a file-backed install-root predicate cannot represent it. v18 deletes that rule and weakens the remaining statement to the one-way condition that PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED may be used only for listed classes.

Every signed entry may still choose any member of the closed volumeConstraint union, and resolutionPredicate branches solely on the chosen tag. No live v18 rule requires an OS ABI entry to choose PATHLESS or forbids it from choosing INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME or EXTERNAL-ORIGIN, so the newly claimed running-kernel subject check is bypassable.

Even when PATHLESS is selected, pathlessObservation.subject has no closed scalar or object grammar, serialization, or observation interface. It points to subjectByScheme, whose codesign value is only 'the running kernel / OS ABI identity the platform codesign result authenticates' and whose package-db value is only 'the running kernel / OS ABI package the package-db result authenticates.' Those descriptions do not identify which fields or bytes are signed and compared.

observedAttestation retains {scheme,payload}, but neither payload contains the pathless subject and no retained platform result mechanically relates cdhash or package name/version/digest to the untyped subject. The binding sentence therefore depends on the undefined relation it is supposed to close.
blockers.impact: A mandatory OS-ABI cell can qualify without exercising the pathless running-kernel evidence at all, while implementations that do exercise it can sign and observe different subject encodings. This defeats the mandatory taxonomy-cell proof and permits divergent allow/refuse outcomes across otherwise conforming implementations.
blockers.requiredRepair: Restore the normative rule that every OS ABI entry MUST use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED and MUST NOT use either other volume tag. Define a closed, canonically serialized subject variant for each attestation scheme, name the trusted platform observation that produces it, and retain an exact per-scheme success/binding result joining that subject to observedAttestation and the signed pathlessObservation; unknown, failed, ambiguous, or mismatched values must refuse.

shouldFix.title: PLATFORM-ATTESTED still has a second observed schema and an unresolved companion exception to identical forms
evidence: signedForm and observedForm are byte-for-byte equal as JSON objects and remove the equivalent escape, repairing the principal v17 discriminant defect.

The unchanged loaderTraces.identitySerializations.observedAttestation remains a separate normative observed schema. It has different field paths and descriptions: the new form defines a digest of package bytes and a codesign value returned by the platform, while the loader schema retains only generic 40-hex SHA-1 and 64-hex SHA-256 descriptions. Nothing aliases, supersedes, or requires this second object to equal PLATFORM-ATTESTED.observedForm.
sameSerialization consequently claims 'There is no second path' while retained events and evidenceJoin still name observedAttestation through that second loaderTraces path.

The unchanged companion rule permits sonameAbi inside a signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED libc payload, while the new extras-rejected payload variants enumerate only cdhash or name/version/digest and sameSerialization says signed and observed objects are identical. The observed companion is instead required as a separate companionObservation and explicitly not nested under taggedEvidenceForm. The subject does not state whether the optional signed field is an exception to payload closure or how the supposedly identical observed form omits it.
shouldFix.impact: Producers can choose different observed schemas or disagree on whether a lawful libc companion violates the closed payload. Exact signed-to-observed equality remains implementation-defined for PLATFORM-ATTESTED events even though the two newly added core form objects match.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make loaderTraces.identitySerializations.observedAttestation an explicit reference to the single PLATFORM-ATTESTED observed form, or remove it and name the canonical object everywhere. Define one authenticity-core serialization and state exactly how the signed-only sonameAbi metadata is excluded from that core while companionObservation remains separate; retain extras rejection for every other field.

shouldFix.title: The retained setns verifier pair is not joined to the run-level observer identity
evidence: setnsObservation now retains mountinfoBytes, hashes them, derives linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity and filesystemTypeToken from those exact bytes, and records ordered verifier and held-namespace before/after observations. This repairs the digest-only and replayability defects from v17.

verifierAfter MUST equal verifierBefore, but neither nested value is required to equal runPreselectionRecord.observerProcessIdentity. observerProcessIdentityShape merely calls the outer value the verifier, and evidenceJoin.runBinding does not add the missing field equality.

The outer observerProcessIdentity is the run identity carried by the closed preselection record and later event schema, while the nested pair is the process around which the namespace helper proof is ordered. A syntactically valid record can therefore name process X outside setnsObservation and prove the before/after invariant for process Y inside it.
The namespace side has a transitive join through mountNamespaceIdentityShape, receivedNsfdInode, helperPostSetnsNsInode, and heldNsInodeBefore/After; the parallel verifier-process join is absent.
shouldFix.impact: The replayable mountinfo proof need not belong to the verifier identity that labels the qualification run. That breaks the retained association between the run, the held namespace, and the helper observation without violating any explicit equality rule.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require setnsObservation.verifierBefore and verifierAfter to equal runPreselectionRecord.observerProcessIdentity under one closed {pid,starttime} serialization, and require later run bindings to use that same value. Refuse any mismatch.

advisories.title: resolverObservation uses an undefined path projection from object identity
advisories.evidence: The new trusted-sensor record captures a path from the same resolution operation and closes canonicalPath-to-actualOrigin-to-signedOrigin equality, which repairs the operational v17 gap. It additionally says resolvedObjectIdentity 'projects' to the canonical path, but resolvedObjectIdentity still has no closed shape or projection function; content identities can also correspond to more than one path.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The same-resolution trusted-sensor capture and exact three-way path equality provide the decisive origin binding even without deriving a path from the authenticity identifier itself. The undefined projection phrase is redundant rather than the sole security join.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Replace the projection wording with an exact same-resolution or same-open-object association token, or define the retained object-handle identity and path projection explicitly.
